'''Oleg V. Minin''' ({{langx|ru|link=no|Олег Владиленович Минин}}) was born on 22 March 1960 in [[Novosibirsk]], [[Akademgorodok|Academytown]], Russia. He is a Russian [[physicist]], a corresponding member of the Russian Academy of Metrology, and a full professor of Physics at the [[Tomsk Polytechnic University]]. He is renowned for his contributions to creating new scientific directions, including THz 3D [[Zone plate]], Mesatronics ([[Mesoscopic physics|mesoscale photonics]]), hyper cumulative [[shaped charge]], [[Structured light|subwavelength structured light]], encompassing [[acoustics]] and surface [[plasmon]].

==Biography==
Oleg V. Minin obtained his M.S. from [[Novosibirsk State University]] in 1982. He earned his PhD in [[Candidate of Sciences|physics and mathematics]] from the [[V.E. Zuev Institute of Atmospheric Optics|Tomsk Institute of Atmospheric Optics]] in 1987, specialising in radiophysics and quantum physics.<ref name="Karabchevsky">Alina Karabchevsky, [https://ab74d9ba-18a8-4d17-a106-49945088baf9.filesusr.com/ugd/12ada6_d4291fe0230149849d05f8855e3875bc.pdf ''Development of mesoscale photonics and plasmonics: a tribute to the jubilee of Professors Igor V. Minin and Oleg V. Minin''], SPIE Photonics Europe, 2020.</ref> During this period, he also worked part-time as a laboratory assistant at the Institute of Applied Physics ([[Novosibirsk]], [[Akademgorodok|Academytown]]), founded by his father, scientist [[Vladilen F. Minin]], in 1966.

In March 2004, Oleg defended his doctoral thesis at the [[Novosibirsk State Technical University]] and was awarded the degree of Doctor of Technical Sciences, equivalent to a [[Habilitation#Equivalent degrees|Habilitation degree]].

His dissertation, which received recognition from the [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)]] for the best scientific work during 1997-2000, served as the foundation for several monographs, including "Diffraction Optics of Millimetre Waves,"<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.routledge.com/Diffractional-Optics-of-Millimetre-Waves/Minin-Minin/p/book/9780367454326 | title=Diffractional Optics of Millimetre Waves }}</ref> "Basic Principles of Fresnel Antenna Arrays,"<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9783540795582 | title=Basic Principles of Fresnel Antenna Arrays }}</ref> and later, "Diffractive Optics and Nanophotonics: Resolution Below the Diffraction Limit,"<ref>{{cite book | url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-319-24253-8 | doi=10.1007/978-3-319-24253-8 | title=Diffractive Optics and Nanophotonics | series=SpringerBriefs in Physics | year=2016 | isbn=978-3-319-24251-4 | last1=Minin | first1=Igor | last2=Minin | first2=Oleg | bibcode=2016don..book.....M }}</ref> and "The Photonic Hook: From Optics to Acoustics and Plasmonics."<ref>{{cite book | url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-66945-4 | doi=10.1007/978-3-030-66945-4 | title=The Photonic Hook | series=SpringerBriefs in Physics | year=2021 | isbn=978-3-030-66944-7 | last1=Minin | first1=Oleg V. | last2=Minin | first2=Igor V. | bibcode=2021phho.book.....M | s2cid=234285298 }}</ref> In 2007, his biographical data was included in [[Marquis Who's Who]] in the World.<ref name="Karabchevsky"/> Almost all of Oleg's scientific work was conducted with his [[List of twins#Scientists|twin brother]], [[Igor V. Minin]].

In April 2007, a book dedicated to the 40th anniversary of the Novosibirsk Institute of Applied Physics led to accusations by the [[Federal Security Service|FSB of Russia]] that Oleg and his brother Igor had revealed sensitive information about projects conducted at an institute that conducts research for the [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)]].<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2007/08/27/world/europe/27iht-moscow.1.7268656.html ''Russia arrests 10 suspects in  murder of reporter''], "New York Times", August 27, 2007.</ref><ref>Alexandra Taranova, [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2010/09/21/2-scientists-held-in-murky-spy-case-a1622 ''2 Scientists Held in Murky Spy Case''], "Moscow Times", September 21, 2010; Natalya Krainova, [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2012/11/13/physicist-convicted-of-espionage-gets-parole-a19345 ''Physicist Convicted of Espionage Gets Parole''], "Moscow Times", November 13, 2012.</ref> This case gained significant public attention, and well-known scientists and human rights activists came forward to defend the physics brothers. However, in July of the same year, the FSB investigators dropped the charges against Oleg and Igor, and prosecutors in [[Novosibirsk]] issued a rare apology to the scientists.{{Citation needed|date=November 2020}}

==Research==
O.V. Minin has established strong research foundations in various fields of physics, holding global priority in areas such as shock wave focusing using diffractive optics,<ref>[https://www.intechopen.com/profiles/3712/oleg-minin Novosibirsk State Technical University. Oleg Minin]</ref> explosive [[plasma antenna]]s, near-field [[Structured light|subwavelength structured light]], mesoscale acoustic [[lens]]es, and hyper cumulative [[shaped charge]].

In collaboration with his twin brother, [[Igor V. Minin]], in 2015, he discovered the so-called photonic hook effect in optics, plasmonics, and acoustics.<ref>{{Cite book |doi = 10.1007/978-3-319-24253-8|title = Diffractive Optics and Nanophotonics|series = SpringerBriefs in Physics|year = 2016|isbn = 978-3-319-24251-4 | last1=Minin | first1=Igor | last2=Minin | first2=Oleg | bibcode=2016don..book.....M }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book |doi = 10.1007/978-3-030-66945-4|title = The photonic hook: from Optics to Acoustics and Plasmonics| series=SpringerBriefs in Physics |year = 2021|isbn = 978-3-030-66945-4 | last1=Minin | first1=Oleg V. | last2=Minin | first2=Igor V. | s2cid=234285298 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1= Dholakia | first1=K. | last2= Bruce | first2=G.D. | title= Optical hooks | journal=  Nature Photonics| volume=13 | date=2019 | issue=4 | doi=10.1038/s41566-019-0403-9| pages=229–230| bibcode=2019NaPho..13..229D | s2cid=256704583 }}</ref> This effect involves artificially curving a light beam with subwavelength curvature and beam waist. Additionally, they experimentally verified the existence of [[surface plasmon]] photonic jet and photonic hook phenomena.<ref name=":0" />

In dielectric structures with Mie size parameter on the order of ten, which lie between wave and [[geometrical optics]], O.V. Minin and his colleagues discovered new and unusual effects, including high-order [[Fano resonance]] in dielectric mesoscale particles, also known as the super-resonance effect.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V. | title= The Superresonance: The Discovery That Was Not Done More Than One Hundred Years Ago | journal= Atmospheric and Oceanic Optics | volume=37 (3)| date=2024 | issue= | doi=10.1134/S1024856024700544| pages=293–301}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1= Wang | first1=Z. | last2=Luk'yanchuk| first2=B. | last3=Yue | first3=L. | last4= Yan | first4=B. | last5=Yan | first5=B. | last6= Monks | first6=J. | last7= Dhama| first7=R. | last8=Minin | first8=O.V.| last9=Minin| first9=I.V.| last10=Huang| first10=S.| last11=Fedyanin| first11=A. | title=High order Fano resonances and giant magnetic fields in dielectric microspheres | journal= Scientific Reports| volume=9 | date=2019 | issue=1 | doi=10.1038/s41598-019-56783-3 | doi-access=free| page=20293| pmid=31889112 | pmc=6937277 | bibcode=2019NatSR...920293W }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.| last3=Zhou | first3=S. | title=High-Order Fano Resonance in a Mesoscale Dielectric Sphere with a Low Refractive Index | journal= JETP Letters| volume=116 | date=2022 | issue=3 | doi= 10.1134/S002136402260121X | pages=144–148| bibcode=2022JETPL.116..144M | s2cid=252820910 }}</ref> This effect allows for the generation of giant magnetic and electric fields particles compared with the magnetic field in [[Neutron star]].

With his colleagues also pioneered the study of the unusual optical properties of superresonance and photonic hooks in and near a rotating dielectric sphere,<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Tang | first1=H. | last2=Shi | first2=Z.| last3=Li | first3=R. |  last4=We | first4=B. | last5=Gong | first5=S.| last6=Minin | first6=I.V. | last7=Minin | first7=O.V. | title= Unusual Optical Phenomena Inside and Near a Rotating Sphere: the Photonic Hook and Resonance | journal= Optics Express | volume=32 (7)| date=2024 | issue= | doi= 10.1364/OE.518794 | pages= 12950–12966 | doi-access=free }}</ref> based on the analogue of optical [[Magnus effect]]. With his brother, he also founded the new field of "[[freezing]] droplet optics" with the discovery of unusual time domain effects of Fano resonancesand photonic hook.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=O.V. | last2=Minin | first2=I.V.|  last3=Cao | first3=Y. | title=Time Domain Self-bending Photonic Hook Beam Based on Freezing Water Droplet | journal= Scientific Reports | volume=13 | date=2023 | doi= 10.1038/s41598-023-34946-7 | page=7732 | doi-access=free | pmc=10182040 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.| last3=Zhou | first3=S. | last4=Luk'yanchuk | first4=B.| title= High order Fano resonance in the time domain for a freezing water microdroplet | journal= Scientific Reports | volume=13 | date=2024 | doi= 10.1038/s41598-024-74425-1 | page=24118 | doi-access=free | pmc=11480091 }}</ref>

The presence of these unusual properties and applications indicates the formation of a promising new direction in optics called "Mesotronics".<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.| title=Mesotronics: Some New, Unusual Optical Effects | journal=Photonics | volume=9 | date=2022 | issue=10 | doi=10.3390/photonics9100762 | page=762 | bibcode=2022Photo...9..762M | doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Minin | first1=I.V. | last2=Minin | first2=O.V.| last3= Luk'yanchuk| first3=B.| editor-first1=Igor V. | editor-first2=Sylvain | editor-first3=Vasily N. | editor-last1=Minin | editor-last2=Lecler | editor-last3=Astratov | title= Mesotronic era of dielectric photonics | volume=121520D | date=2022 | doi= 10.1117/12.2634133| page=762| bibcode=2022SPIE12152E..0DM | isbn=978-1-5106-5180-7 | s2cid=248641915 }}</ref>

O.V. Minin conducted pioneering investigations of plasma jets produced by intense laser-matter interactions based on hyperaccumulation principles.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Baranov | first1=P.F. | last2=Zatonov | first2=I.A.| title=Some pioneering research in laboratory simulation of scaled astrophysical phenomena by Russian physicists | journal= Journal of Physics: Conference Series| volume=1709 | date=2020 | issue=1 | doi=10.1088/1742-6596/1709/1/012003| article-number=012003| bibcode=2020JPhCS1709a2003B | s2cid=234566394 | doi-access=free }}</ref> This research aims to understand better [[astrophysical jet]]s, as cumulative jets are observed to originate from [[young stellar object]]s and [[Active galactic nucleus|active galactic nuclei]]. The findings also provide insight into [[shock wave]]s.

O.V. Minin is the author or co-author of over 150 patents in the [[Russia|USSR/Russia]] and has contributed to about 450 research publications, including 22 monographs (12 in Russian, 9 in English, and 1 in Chinese).<ref name="Karabchevsky" /> 

==Awards==
* O.V. Minin received the medal of the Russian National Committee on Theoretical and Applied Mechanics of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]], named after Kh.A. Rakhmatulin, in 2013 for his contribution to the theory of hyperaccumulation.<ref>Medal Award List
named after Kh.A. Rakhmatulin [http://volnogaz.math.msu.su/pages/medal1.php]</ref>

* Additionally, he has been awarded Russian medals named after V.I. Vernadsky and A. Nobel.<ref name="Karabchevsky"/>
